paragraphs: Friend, here's what sticks with me. Josiah had done so much right. He set the temple in order, and then he got a warning he didn't take. Neco told him, "God has told me to hurry," and the passage says Josiah "did not listen to Neco's words from the mouth of God" (2 Chronicles 35:21-22).

So the lesson is not "Josiah was a bad king." The lesson is that a good record doesn't mean we can stop listening. I think it's easy to coast on what we did yesterday, and I've coasted on a good batch myself. Listening to God is something we keep doing, even when the voice comes from somewhere we didn't expect.

And look at how Josiah is remembered. All Judah and Jerusalem mourned for him, Jeremiah the prophet lamented over him, and his "deeds of loving devotion according to what is written in the Law of the LORD" were written down (2 Chronicles 35:24-26). Friend, that is a record worth wanting. One hard ending didn't erase the loving devotion. Keep listening, keep baking, and let your days be the kind somebody writes down. The story of Josiah's reign is finished, but yours is still in the oven.
